scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: host_1_1_1_1 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: host_1_1_1_1's correct gateway is 10.1.1.1 (switch_dist_1_1's br0
  address). Its default route was repointed to 10.1.1.254 -- in-subnet but
  unassigned -- so ARP for the gateway never resolves and no off-subnet
  packet leaves the host. On-link destinations (10.1.1.1 via the connected
  route) still work, which is why the gateway pings fine. DNS "times out"
  only because the resolver 10.200.0.2 is off-subnet. The network itself is
  healthy: pod 2 reaches everything, and switch_dist_1_1 still advertises
  10.1.1.0/24.
Localization: host_1_1_1_1
Root cause: host_1_1_1_1's default gateway set to 10.1.1.254 instead of
  10.1.1.1
Fix: restore the default route on host_1_1_1_1 --
  `ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scenario.fix_spec:
restore host_1_1_1_1's default route --
`ip route replace default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: default gateway / default route points at wrong address (10.1.1.254 instead of 10.1.1.1)
bonus-exonerates-network: notes switch_dist_1_1 and the OSPF core are healthy (pod 2 works, the real gateway answers), so no network device needs fixing

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: host_1_1_1_1’s IP routing configuration (default gateway) on eth0. 

Mechanism: The host has a default route pointing to a non-existent next hop 10.1.1.254. For any off-subnet traffic (e.g., 10.200.0.0/24 servers and 10.2.1.0/24 pod), the kernel tries to ARP for 10.1.1.254, fails, and returns “Destination Host Unreachable” locally. This also breaks DNS, since queries to 10.200.0.2 cannot be forwarded.

Localization: 
- On host_1_1_1_1: “ip route” shows “default via 10.1.1.254 dev eth0”; “ip neigh” shows “10.1.1.254 … FAILED”; pings to off-subnet addresses return from 10.1.1.2 “Destination Host Unreachable”. The host can ping 10.1.1.1 because it is an on-subnet neighbor (confirmed by successful ping).
- On the gateway side, switch_dist_1_1’s br0 is 10.1.1.1/24 and has OSPF-learned routes to all networks, confirming 10.1.1.1 is the correct default gateway for this subnet. The rest of the fabric is healthy (host_2_1_1_1 reaches servers and DNS normally).

Root cause: Misconfigured default gateway on host_1_1_1_1 set to 10.1.1.254 instead of the actual gateway 10.1.1.1.

Corrective fix: Update host_1_1_1_1 to use 10.1.1.1 as its default route. Example:
- ip route del default; ip route add default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0
Also correct the persistent network configuration (e.g., /etc/network/interfaces, netplan, or NetworkManager) so the default gateway remains 10.1.1.1 across reboots. After change, off-subnet pings and DNS lookups should succeed.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies host_1_1_1_1 as the affected device and attributes the issue to its misconfigured default gateway on eth0.

Recommends changing the default route to via 10.1.1.1 on eth0 and updating persistent network config, which matches the expected fix.
